chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'so let him eat reasonably.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The reasonableness is the daily bread, and it refers to the executor or the custodian regarding their wealth, and what is correct for them.'

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفُ: Reasonableness / Fairness / What is customary and good

ai.seo_question: What does 'eating reasonably' mean for an orphan's custodian in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Quranic command for orphans' custodians to 'eat reasonably' by defining 'al-ma'ruf' as the necessary sustenance (qut) appropriate to the custodian's status and needs. It specifically contextualizes the verse as addressing the guardian managing the orphan's assets, ensuring that consumption is neither excessive nor insufficient, thereby balancing the custodian's livelihood with the preservation of the orphan's wealth.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:6] so let him eat reasonably. Heasws said: ‘The reasonableness, it is the daily bread, and rather it means the executor or the custodian regarding their wealth, and what is correct for them’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from all from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

About the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘He must eat to the proper limit’, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Al-Ma‘ruf (proper limit) is what one needs for sustenance. It applies to the executor of the will or one who is appointed as the custodian of their assets and to work for their welfare.’”
